changes.before: Complete errorReply(error). For an error with code INVALID_INPUT return status 400 and body.error "Check the supplied values". All other errors return status 500 and body.error "Something went wrong". Do not return the internal error message or stack.
changes.after: Send a useful error message without revealing private server details.

before: A request can fail because of invalid input or an unexpected server problem. Those failures need different responses.
An HTTP 400 response tells the caller to correct the request. A 500 response indicates an unexpected server failure.
An internal error can contain file paths, database details, or secrets. Do not send its message or stack directly to a client.
This prints true. The code is used for a decision, while the internal message stays private.
Express error-handling middleware has four parameters: error, request, response, and next. The four-parameter form identifies its job.
If headers have already been sent, forward the error instead of trying to send a second response.
In this practice, errorReply only chooses safe response data. The browser does not run an Express server.
The supplied companion middleware calls your function, applies its status, and sends its body. Test actual routes separately before treating a server integration as verified.
after: Some requests fail because their input is invalid. Others fail because the server has an unexpected problem. Give the caller a clear response for the kind of failure.
Status 400 asks the caller to correct the request. Status 500 reports an unexpected server failure. Hiding private details does not turn a failure into success.
An internal error message or stack can reveal file paths, database details, or secrets. A stack lists where the program was running when it failed. Keep those details out of the response.
Match the exact known code INVALID_INPUT. Optional access, ?., lets the check handle a missing error value. Every other case uses the general server-error response.
Create a separate response object containing only the required public fields. Do not copy the incoming error object, message, or stack into it.
An Express error handler has four parameters: error, req, res, and next. Place it after routes that may fail. The supplied local handler calls errorReply and sends its chosen status and body.
If response headers were already sent, the local handler forwards the error with next(error). It must not try to send another complete response.
Complete errorReply with the two specified statuses and messages. Keep the wording exact so callers and checks can recognize the response.
The browser checks response selection only. A local route test must also confirm what the real server sends. Keep detailed diagnostics in restricted server logs with secrets removed.

before.question: A database failure includes an internal password in error.message. What should the client receive?
choices: The full message so it can debug the database.
A generic server-error response, without the password.
Status 200 because hiding the message means success.
before.explanation: Unexpected failures still need an error status, but private diagnostic details must not be copied into the public response.

after.question: A database error's message contains a password. What should the caller receive?
choices: A general server-error response without the password
Status 200 because the details are hidden
after.explanation: Report the failure while keeping private diagnostic details out of the response.
